The correct answer is involuntary manslaughter: the defendant intended only a battery (a slight wound), not a felony or serious bodily harm, so malice is not implied and the killing is not murder. Because the death resulted from an unlawful act not amounting to a felony and without malice, it is involuntary manslaughter rather than voluntary manslaughter (no heat of passion or adequate provocation).  
CONFIDENCE: 85
